{"filepath":"improvement_proposals.md","content":"# Improvement Proposals — "Make it better"
Date: 2026-09-06
Prepared by: Creative & Documentation Specialist

Purpose
- Deliver 2–3 concrete, prioritized improvement proposals (design/content/workflow/feature) that map to the research and baseline work already delivered. These are ready for engineering and stakeholders: each proposal includes expected effects on the defined metrics, implementation steps, rough effort, dependencies, and explicit acceptance / QA criteria.

Notes
- I built these proposals using Alice’s research_findings.md and Bob’s baseline_metrics.md. Those files contain detailed references, measurement queries and instrumentation requirements; this doc assumes the team will provide analytics / staging access described in Bob’s handoff so we can capture baselines and run A/B tests.

Prioritization (recommended)
1. Performance & Third‑Party Optimization (Quick wins) — Highest urgency and ROI
2. Checkout Flow Simplification & Conversion Reliability — Medium term, high business impact
3. Accessibility + Automated QA Pipeline — Parallel investment, medium effort, reduces legal & churn risk

Proposal 1 — Performance & Third‑Party Optimization (Quick Wins)
Goal
- Reduce page load friction and third‑party overhead to improve Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP/FID, CLS) and thereby increase conversion and reduce bounce rates.
Why prioritized
- Page speed improvements are low-to-medium effort with consistently high conversion uplift in industry studies; this is the fastest route to measurable revenue impact.
Expected effect on metrics (estimates)
- LCP: reduce 75th percentile for key pages by 30–60% (target: <2.5s on mobile for top landing/product pages)
- INP/FID: reduce to <200ms for interactive input on key flows
- CLS: reduce to <0.10 for core pages
- Conversion rate: relative uplift 3–10% in early A/B tests; cart abandonment down 3–8% across funnel (varies by baseline)

Implementation steps (engineering-focused)
1. Instrumentation (0.5–1 week, prerequisite)
   - Ensure RUM is collecting Core Web Vitals by page and device (75th percentiles); confirm synthetic monitoring (Lighthouse) for top 20 pages as Bob recommended.
   - Add feature flagging for progressive rollout of changes.
2. Static asset optimizations (1–2 weeks, low effort)
   - Convert large images to AVIF/WebP and provide responsive srcset.
   - Ensure images have width/height attributes and use modern lazy-loading techniques for offscreen images.
   - Compress and minify CSS/JS; enable Brotli/Gzip on CDN.
3. Critical CSS & render-path (2–5 days)
   - Extract and inline critical CSS for top landing/product pages; defer non-critical styles.
4. Third‑party script audit & defer (3–7 days)
   - Audit all tags/scripts; identify non-essential scripts to defer or load async (analytics, chat widgets, ad pixels).
   - Move consent/marketing tags behind consent manager or lazy load at interaction.
5. Caching & CDN (1 week)
   - Confirm CDN edge caching rules; set long TTLs for immutable assets, cache HTML at edge where safe; configure cache purging.
6. Optional: Server/edge rendering and code-splitting (medium scope)
   - If single-page app is causing hydrating delays, implement partial SSR/edge rendering for product and checkout entry pages (estimate: medium effort, multi-sprint).

Rough effort
- Low for the prioritized quick wins (2–4 weeks of focused frontend/infra work). Additional medium work for SSR/edge rendering (2–6 sprints).

Dependencies
- Read-only access to analytics / BigQuery or CSV exports (Bob’s access instructions)
- Staging environment with feature flags and CI/CD
- List of third‑party vendors and tag manager access

Acceptance / QA criteria (must be measurable)
- Observability: RUM and Lighthouse synthetic monitors are running and reporting for top 20 pages before starting.
- Performance targets (post‑deployment A/B or canary):
  - LCP (75th percentile, mobile) on top landing/product pages decreases by >=30% and is <2.5s.
  - INP/FID (75th percentile) <200ms on target pages.
  - CLS (75th percentile) <0.10.
  - Lighthouse Performance score improvement: +10 points minimum (or reach >=90 on desktop / >=70 on mobile depending on baseline).
- Business impact (30 days after rollout or via A/B test):
  - Measured increase in conversion rate of at least 3% relative (or a statistically significant uplift at p<=0.05 if A/B testing).
  - Cart abandonment reduction measurable and consistent with site-wide trends; target >=3% relative reduction.

Rollout & monitoring
- Implement in a feature-flagged canary (5–10% traffic), monitor RUM and error logs for 48–72 hours, then ramp.
- Run A/B test (if feasible) for primary conversion pages for 2–4 weeks or until statistical significance.

Risk & rollback
- Risk: CDN misconfiguration or asset breakage. Rollback by disabling the feature flag / CDN rule and purge caches.

Proposal 2 — Checkout Flow Simplification & Conversion Reliability
Goal
- Reduce friction in the checkout funnel to decrease abandonment and increase completed orders and revenue.
Why prioritized
- Checkout is highest business-impact area; improvements produce direct revenue gains. Alice’s research and industry benchmarks indicate high ROI for simplification.
Expected effect on metrics (estimates)
- Checkout completion rate: improve absolute +3–8% (relative uplift 5–20% possible depending on baseline)
- Cart abandonment: reduce by 5–15% in the funnel steps improved
- Average order value (AOV): small potential uplift if page speed and trust signals improve

Implementation steps (cross-functional)
1. Measure & map (1 week)
   - Use Bob’s funnel queries (GA4 => BigQuery) to identify largest drop-off steps and compute baseline conversion by step.
   - Capture session replays and usability heuristics for top rejection points.
2. Quick UX fixes (2–4 weeks)
   - Add guest checkout if not present; highlight trust signals (security badges, clear cost breakdown).
   - Reduce form fields: avoid unnecessary address confirmations, auto-complete, and use address validation API.
   - Inline validation and client-side checks to avoid expensive round-trips.
   - Add progress indicator and one-click edit for cart items without going back several pages.
3. Payment & technical reliability (2–6 weeks)
   - Integrate optimized payment methods (e.g., native wallets, accelerated checkout) prioritized by analytics.
   - Harden idempotency on order submission; handle network timeouts with retry logic and user-friendly states (do not duplicate orders).
   - Ensure server-side performance for checkout endpoints (make them high priority for caching and autoscaling).
4. Experimentation & rollout (3–8 weeks)
   - Implement changes behind flags and design A/B tests for checkout completion.
   - Run experiments on segments with highest traffic.

Rough effort
- Medium (3–8 sprints depending on how many technical changes & payment integrations are needed).

Dependencies
- Payment provider documentation and sandbox access
- Analytics event data and BigQuery access for funnel metrics
- UX resources for flow redesign and copywriting

Acceptance / QA criteria
- Functional correctness: no duplicated orders; successful order webhook/payment reconciliation pass rate >=99.5% in staging before rollout.
- Conversion targets: Checkout completion rate increases by at least 3% absolute OR experiment shows statistically significant uplift (p<=0.05) within the test period.
- Funnel metrics: Specific step(s) with prior largest drop show a relative reduction in drop-off by >=10%.
- Performance: Checkout entry page maintains LCP and INP targets from Proposal 1.
- Regression checks: Payment and order reconciliation logs show no increase in failures beyond normal variance (define baseline from analytics).

Rollout & monitoring
- Feature-flagged rollout; monitor payment success rate, error rates, and GA4 funnel events. Keep kill switch on payment flows.

Proposal 3 — Accessibility & Automated QA Pipeline
Goal
- Achieve a clear, repeatable path to WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for core flows and add automated checks into CI to prevent regressions.
Why prioritized
- Improves usability for more users, reduces legal risk, improves SEO and conversion. Automated checks reduce future rework.
Expected effect on metrics (estimates)
- Accessibility non-compliance issues reduced to near-zero for automated checks; manual audit pass on core flows.
- Small but measurable improvement in conversion/engagement for assistive-tech users and improvements in SEO visibility over time.

Implementation steps
1. Automated scanning in CI (1–2 weeks)
   - Integrate axe-core / pa11y / lighthouse accessibility checks into CI for pull requests; fail builds on defined thresholds.
2. High‑priority manual remediation (3–6 weeks)
   - Run automated scans across top 20 pages; triage issues into critical/high/medium.
   - Fix top critical issues (form labels, keyboard focus order, aria attributes, contrast, alt text, semantic headings).
3. Manual verification (2 weeks)
   - Conduct a manual WCAG 2.1 AA check on core purchase and account flows (2–3 key user journeys).
   - Engage QA with assistive tech tests (screen reader + keyboard only) on staging.
4. Documentation & training (ongoing)
   - Add accessible components to design system, include usage docs, PR checklist for accessibility.

Rough effort
- Medium (3–8 weeks for initial remediation and CI pipeline); ongoing smaller effort for maintenance.

Dependencies
- Access to staging environment and list of top pages (from research and analytics)
- Design system ownership and front-end engineering time

Acceptance / QA criteria
- Automated CI checks run on every PR and must not regress: axe critical issues must be reduced by >=90% on top pages compared to baseline scan.
- Manual audit: core flows (checkout, account creation, product discovery) pass WCAG 2.1 AA checklist items for keyboard navigation and screen-reader readability.
- No critical accessibility violations in production for top 10 revenue pages (verified by automated scans + manual sampling).

Rollout & monitoring
- Automate scans weekly in staging and daily synthetic checks for production top pages.

Measurement plan (cross-proposal)
- Baseline capture: Run the BigQuery/GA4 queries and Lighthouse/RUM reports Bob outlined immediately to lock baselines for conversion, cart abandonment and Core Web Vitals.
- For all proposals, use A/B testing (recommended) or feature-flagged canary rollouts; use the same duration and statistical methodology across experiments.
- Primary KPIs: conversion rate, checkout completion, cart abandonment, LCP (75th), INP/FID (75th), CLS (75th), Lighthouse score, and accessibility violations (axe counts).

Suggested short timeline (first 8 weeks)
- Week 0: Provide analytics & staging access (per Bob). Run baseline capture.
- Weeks 1–3: Implement Proposal 1 quick wins + CI accessibility checks. Launch canary and monitor.
- Weeks 3–8: Implement checkout simplifications (Proposal 2) in parallel with accessibility remediation (Proposal 3). Run experiments.

Owners & roles
- Product Owner: decide experiment targets and business thresholds
- Engineering (Frontend/Platform): implement code changes, CDN, server tweaks
- UX/Design: wireframes for checkout simplification, accessible components
- Data & Analytics: run baseline queries, set up A/B tests, analyze results (Bob)
- QA: automated checks, manual accessibility testing

Deliverables for engineering handoff (what to expect next)
1. A prioritized backlog (user stories + acceptance criteria) derived from the selected proposals.
2. Read-only analytics access or CSV exports so Bob can populate baselines and run A/B analysis.
3. A staging feature‑flag and deploy plan with a rollback strategy.

Risks & open questions
- We do not have live analytics credentials in this workspace. Bob’s baseline instructions must be followed to capture accurate baselines before A/B tests.
- Payment provider and third‑party vendor limitations may constrain rollout scope and timing.
- If the codebase lacks componentized UI, effort for CSS/asset changes will be higher.

Next recommended actions (decision required)
- Provide read-only analytics / BigQuery / staging credentials (per Bob) so we can capture baselines and start instrumentation.
- Decide whether to (A) run a 3–5 day discovery sprint to finalise backlog and precise estimates, or (B) start a 1‑week implementation sprint for the quick wins (Proposal 1). Alice offered both options in research_findings.md.

Appendix — Measurement queries & tools (references)
- Follow the queries and commands Bob provided in Appendix B for GA4->BigQuery funnel metrics, RUM vitals, and Lighthouse runs.
- Use axe-core in CI, Lighthouse for synthetic checks, and RUM for real user metrics.

---
Prepared for: Engineering & Stakeholders
If you want, I can convert each proposal into a prioritized JIRA backlog (stories + estimates) after we receive analytics/staging access.
"}
